rows.answer: You can carry over up to **5 unused PTO days** into the next calendar year. These carried-over days expire on March 31 of that year [S1].
Carried-over vacation (PTO) days expire on March 31 of the following calendar year [S1].
You need to submit your paid time off (PTO) request at least two weeks in advance for any time off of 3 or more consecutive days, which includes a week off [S3].
The core collaboration hours are from 10:00 to 14:00 in the team's primary time zone, Monday to Friday. Employees must be available during this time to collaborate effectively [S1].

Parental leave is 16 weeks of fully paid leave. Employees are eligible if they have at least 6 months of tenure with the company. The leave can be taken in up to two blocks within 12 months of the birth or adoption [S1].
Your employer requires a doctor's note (medical certificate) only if your sick leave lasts longer than 3 consecutive working days [S1].

You can work remotely from another country for up to 30 days in a calendar year without special approval. If you want to work from another country for more than 30 days, you need to get approval from People Operations due to tax and employment-law implications [S1].

New hires must complete the mandatory security awareness training and the data-handling course within their first 5 business days. If they do not finish these trainings by then, their system access is suspended until completion [S1].

An onboarding buddy should meet the new hire at least twice a week during the first month. This helps the new hire with questions about "how do we do things here" while the manager remains responsible for goals and performance [S1].
The daily meal allowance while travelling for work is $75 per day [S1].
A $4,500 expense must be approved by a Director, according to the approval limits in the Expense and Reimbursement Policy [S1].
No, you do not need to keep the receipt for a $20 taxi ride. Receipts are required only for expenses over $25 according to the expense policy [S1].
The maximum hotel rate in London is $350 per night, as it is classified as a high-cost city in the travel expense policy [S1].

No, you cannot pay for a SaaS subscription directly with your company card. All software purchases, including SaaS subscriptions, must go through the procurement and security review process first. This process includes a security review that can take up to 10 business days and may require a signed data processing agreement if the vendor handles customer data [S2][S3].
A lost or stolen company laptop must be reported to Security within 1 hour. [S1]
The minimum password length is 14 characters, as required by the Information Security Policy [S1].

Customer contracts should be classified as **Confidential** data. They must be handled on a **need-to-know basis** and stored **encrypted at rest and in transit** to ensure security and compliance. Additionally, customer data, including contracts, must never be copied to personal devices, personal cloud storage, or unapproved AI tools [S1].
Access reviews are performed every quarter. Managers review their team's access to Confidential and Restricted systems quarterly and remove access within 24 hours of a role change or departure [S1].
A security review of a new SaaS tool takes up to 10 business days before purchase, especially if the tool processes Internal or higher data [S1].
The onboarding time target for Standard plan customers is 3 business days from contract signature to go-live [S1].

Version 2.0 of the customer onboarding procedure introduced a blocking verification step before workspace provisioning. Specifically:

- Workspaces are no longer provisioned immediately; instead, every new business customer must pass a know-your-business (KYB) verification check first.
- This verification is now a blocking step, meaning provisioning waits for verification to complete.
- This change was made to meet new compliance requirements from enterprise and financial-services customers.
- The expected impact is about half a day added to the median onboarding time.

This change became effective on September 1, 2026 [S1][S2].
When the verification provider returns "manual review," the onboarding specialist collects documents from the customer, and then the Compliance team decides within 2 business days [S1].

The root cause of INC-204 was that the verification client was configured with a 5-second timeout and no retry with backoff. After a volume increase in September, the external provider VeriTrust applied per-tenant rate limiting, causing queued requests to take 6 to 9 seconds. The client gave up on these requests, marking verifications as failed and requiring manual restarts by onboarding specialists [S3].
INC-204 affected 63 new customers who experienced onboarding delays of one or more business days due to identity verification timeouts [S1].

INC-198 was caused by a dependency upgrade that changed the CSV parser's default behavior from encoding auto-detection to strict UTF-8 only. Since the test suite only included UTF-8 encoded fixtures, this regression was not detected before release. As a result, the import service started rejecting CSV files that were not UTF-8 encoded, such as Windows-1252 exports from spreadsheet tools, causing data import failures for customers during onboarding [S1][S3].

No, the CSV import incident did not contribute significantly to the September onboarding slowdown. The impact on August onboarding times was minimal, with the median onboarding time changing by less than 0.1 days. INC-198, which covers the CSV import failures, is explicitly stated as not a significant factor in the September slowdown, which is instead covered by INC-204 [S1].

ADR-012 chose an external provider (VeriTrust) instead of building verification in-house because building in-house would require 4 to 6 months of work plus ongoing maintenance for each country, whereas VeriTrust offered coverage of 40+ countries with fast results in seconds for about 90% of businesses and a per-check pricing model. This allowed meeting the compliance requirement on time without the engineering effort and maintenance burden of country-specific registry integrations [S1][S2][S5].

KYB verification is being moved to an asynchronous queue to prevent provisioning delays caused by the current synchronous design, which makes onboarding directly dependent on VeriTrust's latency and availability. The synchronous approach caused timeouts and outages to block onboarding, as seen in the 12-day degraded service incident in September 2026 (INC-204). Moving to an asynchronous job queue will allow provisioning to resume automatically when verification completes, improving reliability and customer onboarding speed. This change is planned for Q4 2026 as a remediation after the incident [S1][S3][S4].

Support should escalate a cluster of similar tickets to engineering when **more than 10 tickets with the same tag are opened within 48 hours**. This is considered a "ticket cluster" and is a leading indicator of an incident, warranting escalation to the on-call engineer of the owning team [S1].
The first response time for a P2 ticket is 1 hour [S3].

Single sign-on (SSO) is included only in the **Enterprise plan**. This plan supports SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect SSO with major identity providers and allows admins to configure SSO using a setup wizard in under 15 minutes [S1][S3].
SCIM deprovisioning must remove a user's access within 5 minutes. This applies to Enterprise workspaces using the SCIM 2.0 user provisioning and deprovisioning feature [S1][S3].

Customer onboarding slowed down in September 2026 primarily because version 2.0 of the onboarding procedure made identity verification a blocking step, adding about half a day to the median onboarding time. Additionally, from September 8 to September 19, a high timeout rate (up to 22%) occurred on verification requests to the external provider VeriTrust due to rate limiting and a short client timeout setting, causing delays for 63 new customers and a backlog of support tickets [S1][S2][S3][S4].

The first signal of the September verification problem was a rise in support ticket volume related to verification timeouts, which was noticed three days after the issue started. There was no alert on verification timeout rate initially, so the problem was discovered through increased support tickets rather than monitoring [S3][S4].

The home office stipend is a one-time $500 amount for new employees, which must be claimed within 60 days of the start date. To claim it, submit your expenses through the company's expense tool with receipts as proof [S1][S2][S3].
